title: It Shall Never Go Out
subtitle: Sunday — nothing to tend
teaser: Six days of fire. Today there is nothing to add and nothing to keep. Sit near it.
theme: Rest beside a fire that is being kept by somebody else
framework: Leviticus 6:13 — the fire shall ever be burning upon the altar

modules.passage: The fire shall ever be burning upon the altar; it shall never go out.
modules.scriptureContext: The sentence the whole week has been circling. Read it once, slowly, and then put the screen down.

modules.inlineImageAlt: A shallow bed of banked embers on a stone hearth, ash over cracked orange coal, radiating low heat with no flame and nobody attending it
modules.inlineImageCaption: Unattended, and plainly not going out.

modules.heading: Today There Is Nothing to Add
modules.content:
Six days ago we started with a fire that was already burning before anyone arrived to see it.

Since then: a covenant sworn over a sleeping man. A word that means to revive rather than to start. Two lambs a day, and a breakfast given to somebody who had failed. A lamp almost out, in a dark building, on the night God said a boy's name.

Today there is no teaching. There is no exercise. Nothing is being asked.

The altar fire in Israel burned through the night whether or not anyone was watching it. Somebody laid wood on it every morning, and that mattered — but not today, and not you.

So sit near it.

If you have been striving all week to feel something, stop for one day and find out what is still there when you are not working at it. If you missed three days of this and came back for the last one, notice that nothing was withheld from you for it. The fire did not go out while you were away, and there is no penalty to pay before you are allowed near it.

That is the whole of Sunday.

Tomorrow, or whenever you are ready, there will be wood to carry again. Not today.

One line to take into the quiet, if you want one.

The verb in that verse is the same verb God uses in Isaiah when he promises that a smoking wick will not be quenched. The command and the promise are built from the same three letters.

So the thing you were told not to let go out is the thing he has already said he will not put out.

You can rest on that today. It is not your sentence.

modules.prompt: Sit with this one question and do not write an answer. What is still warm?

modules.heading: Silence
modules.instruction: This is the whole practice for today. Most of the day is meant to be this.
steps: Set a timer for five minutes. Longer if you want it, but not shorter.
Sit still. Do not pray in sentences.
When your mind goes to the list, let it go and come back to one line: it shall never go out.
When the timer ends, do not evaluate how it went.

modules.heading: A Prayer for Sunday
modules.prayerText:
Keeper of the fire,

I have nothing to bring today and You have not asked for anything.

It shall never go out. You said that, not me.

Amen.
